learning: No prior race data. Next iteration, compare line_loss_events, rms_error and max_error to decide whether sensor count/spacing or lookahead is the main limit.
notes: Baseline complete robot: Builder's symmetric 5-sensor geometry with a moderate PD-plus-small-I controller and last-direction line recovery. Requests all measurements so the next iteration can separate lookahead, spacing and track-width effects.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback, so the controller is built from the contract and the Builder's baseline geometry. The five sensors at 12 mm spacing with 12 mm footprints overlap slightly, so the line stays visible and the signal changes smoothly. Weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] are kept, since they are proportional to sensor x and positive signal steers left. Signal magnitude is at most 2, and at about 12 mm offset it is roughly 1, so kp=4 gives a turn of about 4 at the edge, a wheel difference of about 2800 PWM. That is strong but not saturating for a moderate error. kd=0.5 damps the oscillation a 0.06 m lookahead can cause, and ki=0.1 is small to avoid integral windup on curves. base_speed=1.6 gives 80 percent PWM, enough to finish the course in under 3 s with margin for turns. line_loss='last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the line instead of stopping or sweeping blindly. Expected result: a completed baseline run with modest line error, which becomes the reference for comparing lookahead and sensor count next iteration.
